stem: Collar cells (choanocytes), which create water currents and trap food, are characteristic of the phylum
explanation: Sponges (Porifera) have choanocytes lining their canals; the beating flagella draw water in through the ostia and the collars trap food particles. Cnidarians have stinging cells instead.

stem: Stinging cells (cnidocytes) containing nematocysts are found in
explanation: Cnidocytes discharge nematocysts to paralyse prey and give the phylum Cnidaria its name. Sponges, earthworms and snails have no stinging cells.

stem: A diploblastic animal is one whose body develops from
explanation: Diploblastic animals such as Hydra have two germ layers, ectoderm and endoderm, with a jelly-like mesoglea between them. Animals with all three layers, including mesoderm, are triploblastic.

stem: Which phylum consists of triploblastic animals that have no body cavity (acoelomates)?
explanation: Flatworms such as the liver fluke and tapeworm have three germ layers, but the space between gut and body wall is filled with mesenchyme. Nematodes have a pseudocoelom, while annelids and arthropods have a true coelom.

stem: Roundworms such as Ascaris are pseudocoelomates because their body cavity
options: is lined by mesoderm on both of its sides
is not completely lined by mesoderm
explanation: A pseudocoelom lies between the mesoderm of the body wall and the endoderm of the gut, so mesoderm lines it on one side only. A true coelom is lined by mesoderm on both sides, and a cavity filled with tissue describes acoelomates.

stem: The earthworm shows a true coelom and a body divided into similar repeated rings. It belongs to the phylum
explanation: Annelids have metameric segmentation, in which the body is divided into similar segments, and a true coelom. Nematodes are unsegmented, and arthropods are segmented but have jointed legs and an exoskeleton.

stem: Jointed appendages and an exoskeleton containing chitin are characteristic features of
explanation: Insects, spiders, crabs and centipedes (arthropods) have a chitinous exoskeleton that they moult and jointed legs. Annelids have no jointed legs and molluscs have a soft body, usually with a shell.

stem: A soft unsegmented body covered by a mantle, which usually secretes a shell, is a feature of the phylum
explanation: Snails, mussels and octopus are molluscs; the mantle is a fold of the body wall that secretes the shell. Echinoderms have an internal skeleton of calcareous plates, not a mantle.

stem: A water vascular system with tube feet, used for movement and feeding, is found in
explanation: Echinoderms such as starfish and sea urchins move water through canals into tube feet, which work by hydraulic pressure. Jellyfish swim by contracting their bell, and octopus uses jet propulsion and arms.

stem: Which set of features is found in all chordates at some stage of their life?
options: Notochord, ventral solid nerve cord and a chitin exoskeleton
Notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord and pharyngeal slits
Dorsal heart, ventral nerve cord and gills
explanation: Every chordate has a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord and pharyngeal gill slits at least in the embryo. A backbone is found only in vertebrates, and a ventral solid nerve cord is typical of non-chordates such as annelids and arthropods.

stem: Bilateral symmetry in animals is closely linked with
options: cephalisation, the concentration of sense organs at the front end
the absence of a nervous system
explanation: A bilaterally symmetrical animal moves head first, so sense organs and nerve cells concentrate at the front (cephalisation). Radial symmetry suits sessile or slow animals such as sea anemones, which meet the environment equally from all sides.

stem: Echinoderms are considered more closely related to chordates than to arthropods because both echinoderms and chordates
options: have jointed limbs and a chitin skeleton
are deuterostomes, in which the blastopore becomes the anus
explanation: In deuterostomes the first embryonic opening (blastopore) becomes the anus and the mouth forms later; arthropods, annelids and molluscs are protostomes, in which the blastopore becomes the mouth. Adult echinoderms are radial, but their larvae are bilateral and they are triploblastic.
